items.followUp: State one way encryption protects information.

rubric.why: Identifies the security purpose of encryption.
rubric.description: States that encryption protects information from unauthorized access.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that encryption prevents unauthorized people from reading or accessing the information.

rubric.why: Shows how encryption helps keep information confidential.
rubric.description: Explains that encryption converts readable data into coded or unreadable form.
rubric.how: Award for stating that plain text is changed into cipher text so its contents remain confidential.

modelAnswer: Encryption protects information from unauthorized access.
It converts readable plain text into coded cipher text, keeping the information confidential.

items.followUp: What is plain text in cryptography?

rubric.why: Identifies cipher text as an encrypted message.
rubric.description: States that cipher text is an encrypted form of a message or data.
rubric.how: Award for describing cipher text as the result of encryption.

rubric.why: Describes how cipher text appears without decryption.
rubric.description: States that cipher text is not normally readable without decryption.
rubric.how: Award for noting that it is coded or unreadable to an unauthorized reader.

modelAnswer: Cipher text is the encrypted form of a message or data.
It is coded and cannot normally be understood without decryption.

items.followUp: What is the binary number system?

rubric.why: Establishes that a number system represents numbers or values.
rubric.description: States that a number system is a method of representing numbers or values.
rubric.how: Award for identifying its purpose as representing numbers or values.

rubric.why: Mentions the symbols used in a number system.
rubric.description: States that a number system uses a set of digits or symbols according to rules.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning its digits or symbols.

modelAnswer: A number system is a way of representing numbers or values.
It uses a set of digits or symbols according to particular rules.

items.followUp: What is the quotient in a division operation?

rubric.why: Connects the remainder to a division operation.
rubric.description: States that a remainder is obtained when one number is divided by another.
rubric.how: Award for correctly relating the remainder to division.

rubric.why: Gives the defining meaning of a remainder.
rubric.description: Explains that it is the amount left after division when the division is not exact.
rubric.how: Award for describing the remainder as what is left over after division.

modelAnswer: A remainder is the amount left over after one number is divided by another.
It occurs when the division is not exact.

items.followUp: Name one type of computer memory and state its use.

rubric.description: States that computer memory stores data, instructions, or information.
rubric.how: Award for naming something that memory stores.

rubric.why: Explains why stored information is needed.
rubric.description: States that stored data or instructions can be used or retrieved by the computer during processing.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that memory makes stored information available for computer use.

modelAnswer: Computer memory is the part of a computer that stores data and instructions.
The computer uses the stored information during processing.

items.followUp: What does ASCII stand for, and what does it do?

accept: american standard code for information interchange
rubric.why: Checks the expansion of the acronym.
rubric.description: Gives the full form of ASCII.
rubric.how: Award for writing American Standard Code for Information Interchange.

rubric.description: Explains that ASCII assigns numerical codes to characters.
rubric.how: Award for stating that it represents characters using numeric codes.

modelAnswer: ASCII stands for American Standard Code for Information Interchange.
It assigns numerical codes to characters.

rubric.why: Checks the first part of the expansion.
rubric.description: Writes “Hypertext” as the first word of HTTP.
rubric.how: Award for the correct word Hypertext.

rubric.why: Checks the remaining words of the expansion.
rubric.description: Writes “Transfer Protocol” as the remaining words of HTTP.
rubric.how: Award for the correct words Transfer Protocol.

modelAnswer: HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol.

items.followUp: Name the main components of a communication system.

rubric.description: Mentions a sender or source that sends the information.
rubric.how: Award for naming the sender or source.

rubric.description: States that a communication system transfers information to a receiver or destination.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning the receiver or destination, or clearly stating that the system transfers information between sender and receiver.

modelAnswer: A communication system is used to send information from a sender to a receiver.
It enables information to be transferred between people or devices.
